prompt: We finished our drone-landing experiments and need to start the journal paper (IEEE-style venue). From the controller source code and the lab notes, draft the Methods section (system description, experimental setup, statistical analysis) and the Results section as LaTeX. Save as paper_sections.tex.
assertions: no-code-identifiers-in-prose: the LaTeX contains none of the source identifiers baro_vision, baro_only, send_velocity_setpoint, mavsdk, ZMQ, EMA_ALPHA, KP_XY, HSV_LOWER, _poll_tag as prose (an academically renamed equivalent must be used)
modes-become-named-controllers: the two config modes appear as two academically named controllers/conditions that serve as the experimental variable of the comparison

constants-tabled-not-prosed: gains, velocity limits, and thresholds appear in a parameter table (symbol/description/value), and internal implementation constants (EMA coefficient, HSV bounds, retry cap, image center pixels) appear nowhere
rate-mismatch-as-argument: the camera-rate vs control-rate mismatch (8 Hz vs 50 Hz) is stated as the reason for the smoothing/hold design (a number carrying an argument), not as bare spec inventory
results-evidence-only: the Results section contains no protocol (placement, operator actions, logging) and no interpretation phrases such as 'which shows that' / 'demonstrates that' / 'confirms'

aggregate-headline-stats: the headline accuracy is aggregate mean±SD touchdown offset; the downwind/upwind direction split is not reported as a headline, and per-trial dropout bookkeeping is not reported as a statistic
quantified-comparison: the comparison between modes is quantified (paired difference with CI, ratio, or percent), not stated as 'better'
ieee-mechanics: no contractions, no prose semicolons, numerals used for numbers 10 and above
